answer: Sybil resistance here comes from a bonded anchor: each agent locks a stake that is slashed when its claims fail peer review, so minting a thousand identities costs a thousand collateral deposits instead of nothing. Voting weight follows the age and diversity of that stake, not raw headcount, and a quartz-timed window forces every new key to answer a fresh challenge before it may vote. Reputation compounds like a sonnet, line by earned line, so a swarm created yesterday carries almost no influence. An attacker flooding keys pays real capital for near-zero weight.
